explanations: terra: A kindled fire lights everything around it, then God removes the people’s نور and leaves them unable to see in darkness; it directly joins fire, illumination, lost sight, and failed guidance.
terra: After the parable’s guiding light is removed in 2:17, the people cannot see or return; their failure to return gives the lost road its moral consequence.
terra: The storm travellers walk whenever lightning illuminates for them and stop when darkness returns, precisely staging movement whose direction depends on intermittent light.
terra: Submitting one’s face to God while doing good yields reward and freedom from fear, turning facial orientation into committed Godward direction.

luna: The ayah says that wherever people turn, there is God's Face; its explicit turning and orientation give spatial force to the source section's dictionary sense of وَجْه as the place one faces. | terra: East and west belong to God, and wherever people turn there is God’s face; every physical heading is encompassed by the face the section’s giver seeks.
terra: When people question the changed direction of prayer, the answer names God as owner of east and west and as guide to a straight path; orientation belongs to the divine Guide.
terra: The former prayer-direction discloses who follows the Messenger and who turns back on his heels, converting bodily orientation into the test of following the leader.
terra: The repeated command to turn one’s face toward the Sacred Mosque gives وَجْه its concrete directional force: the face visibly establishes the course.
terra: The communities refuse one another’s prayer-directions, showing that a visible heading can divide followers when it is detached from revealed guidance.
terra: Every community has a direction toward which it turns, while all are finally gathered by God; distinct headings remain within His encompassing end.
terra: The traveller is commanded, from wherever he sets out, to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque; route, departure, and faced direction are explicit.
terra: The command is extended to everyone wherever they are, making a shared facing the organizing direction of the whole dispersed company.
terra: Followed leaders disown their followers when all see punishment and their bonds are cut, revealing the collapse of the company at its destination.
terra: The followers wish for a return so they can disown their leaders, but they will not emerge from the Fire; reversal of course is desired only after the terminal boundary is crossed.
terra: People insist on following their fathers even when those fathers understood nothing and were not guided; inherited leadership is tested against revelation.
terra: Righteousness is not exhausted by turning faces east or west; the ayah marks the boundary between bodily direction and the deeper seeking of God’s face.

terra: The pilgrimage company moves on from Arafat to the Sacred Monument and remembers God there as He guided them after prior error; a named route-marker and divine guidance meet within an actual journey.
terra: God leads believers from darkness into light, while false patrons lead in the reverse direction and end as companions of the fire; the ayah maps rival guides to opposite termini.

luna: The ayah describes giving for God's sake as seeking His Face (ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ), closely matching the source section's Face as the walker's aim. | terra: Charitable spending counts when it seeks only God’s face, a close parallel to the giver of surah 92 whose gift seeks the face of the Most High.
terra: The Messenger declares that he has submitted his face to God together with those who follow him, combining Godward orientation with a following company.
terra: God rescues a divided people from the brink of a pit of fire; the rim is the boundary where the wrong road ends and saving guidance intervenes.
terra: The community is asked whether it will turn back on its heels if the Messenger dies, exposing the danger that followers reverse course when their leader is no longer visibly ahead.

terra: One who opposes the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows a road other than the believers’ is left to that chosen direction and burned in Hell; alternative following reaches the warning fire.
terra: The best way is attached to one who submits his face to God, does good, and follows Abraham’s upright path, uniting face, way, and following.
terra: After guidance is withheld in 4:168, the only road left is the road of Hell; the exception makes fire the terminal route rather than the saving beacon.
terra: A proof and a clear light are sent down from God, giving the traveller-image a revealed rather than visible form of illumination.
terra: Those who believe in the proof and light of 4:174 and hold fast to God are admitted to mercy and guided to Him on a straight road; the light opens an explicitly Godward path.

luna: A light and a clear Book guide people to paths of peace; the verse concretely brings together the source section's نور/نار illumination note, hidaya, and roads. | terra: A light and clarifying Book are said to have come from God, identifying the illumination by which the paths of 5:16 become visible.
terra: By the revealed light God guides seekers of His pleasure to paths of peace, brings them from darkness into light, and guides them to a straight path.
terra: The Torah is described as containing guidance and light, another revealed joining of the two functions represented by the section’s fire.
terra: The Gospel is likewise described as containing guidance and light, repeating the formula across a second scripture.
terra: The same ancestral appeal is rejected because the fathers possessed neither knowledge nor guidance, repeating the boundary between a prior track and a true guide.

luna: These callers worship their Lord morning and evening while seeking His Face; the source section's Face-seeking walker meets a group whose daily devotion is oriented toward the same divine aim. | terra: Those who call upon their Lord morning and evening desire His face; their repeated worship holds one direction across the day’s two edges.

luna: This ayah pictures a bewildered traveler on earth whose companions call him toward guidance while devils pull him away; its competing directions clarify why the source section's traveler must recognize and follow a true sign. | terra: A bewildered wanderer is drawn away in the earth while companions call, “Come to us,” toward guidance; the scene tests which distant call supplies a true bearing.

luna: Abraham says he has turned his face toward the Creator of the heavens and earth; the source section's dictionary sense of وَجْه as what one faces is bodily orientation here, directed toward God. | terra: Abraham turns his face toward the Creator of the heavens and earth, making the faced object the decisive direction of worship.
terra: Moses’ Book is described as a light and guidance for people, directly uniting the fire scene’s two functions in a nonliteral form.

luna: This ayah gives the section's night-travel function to the stars: they are made as guides through the darknesses of land and sea, much as the distant fire lets a traveler correct direction. | terra: The stars are appointed so people may find their way through the darknesses of land and sea, exactly matching nocturnal orientation by a distant light.

luna: The ayah gives a person light “by which he walks among people” (يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي النَّاسِ), a walking-light counterpart to the traveler who sees a distant fire and sets his direction. | terra: God gives the revived person a light by which he walks among people, opposite one trapped in darkness; light here performs the section’s exact work of making a walkable way.

luna: God identifies His straight path and commands people to follow it, warning against other paths that divide them from it; this makes the source section's road-sign image a choice between staying on a route and straying. | terra: God identifies one straight path, commands people to follow it, and forbids the divergent ways that scatter them; the road is clarified by its forks and boundaries.
terra: Satan vows to sit in ambush on God’s straight road, placing the misleader as an obstruction precisely on the route disclosed by guidance.
terra: People are commanded to set their faces at every place of worship and call on God sincerely, giving the face a repeated devotional heading.

terra: As successive communities enter the Fire, each curses the one before it, and the last accuses the first of leading it astray; front and rear of the human procession meet at the wrong destination.
terra: Lot and his household are saved except his wife, who belongs to those who remain behind; the rescue line is defined by one member’s contrary rear position.
terra: Success belongs to those who follow the Messenger and follow the light sent with him; a leader and a light are jointly followed along the same saving course.
terra: The first forerunners are followed in excellence by later believers, giving the moral community a leading rank and faithful followers.

luna: God calls to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, giving the source section's road-guiding image a defined destination as well as direction. | terra: God calls to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, joining a known home, a caller, and the road leading to it.

luna: The ayah assigns night to rest and day to seeing (مُبْصِرًا), giving the source section's night-and-day travel distinction its practical contrast in visibility. | terra: God makes night for rest and day sight-giving; the description supports the section’s distinction between obscure night travel and naturally visible day travel.
terra: The command to set one’s face firmly toward the upright religion renders fidelity as an unwavering heading.

luna: This second telling of Lot's escape repeats the night departure and no-look-back command, adding that his wife is the exception; it sharpens the boundary between continuing forward and turning back. | terra: The parallel command sends Lot’s family out by night and forbids anyone from looking back, making backward orientation the danger within the ordered escape.

luna: Pharaoh goes ahead of his people and brings them to the Fire. This reverses the source section's guide at the head of a caravan and fire as a warning sign: a leader can take the whole procession to the danger itself. | terra: Pharaoh precedes his people on the Last Day and brings them into the fire; he is a caravan head whose leadership delivers the whole line to the wrong watering place.
terra: The Messenger calls this “my way,” calls to God with insight, and includes those who follow him; a visible course is opened by a leader and continued by followers.
terra: The Messenger is explicitly a warner and every people has a guide; it places warning and guidance side by side just as the section hears both in the warning fire.

luna: These servants seek their Lord's Face and spend from what God provided; the pairing of Face-seeking and giving mirrors the source section's destination for the generous walk. | terra: The steadfast seek their Lord’s face while praying, spending, and repelling evil with good; a life’s actions acquire one governing direction.

luna: The revealed Book brings people from darkness to light and to the path of the Mighty; this gives the source section's night-and-guiding-light image a scriptural path between darkness and disclosure. | terra: The Book is sent so the Messenger may bring people from darkness into light by God’s leave and onto His path, turning revelation into the section’s night-road illumination.

luna: Moses is sent to bring his people from darkness into light, joining the same prophet who sees a night fire in the source section to guidance out of darkness. | terra: Moses is commanded to bring his people from darkness into light and remind them of God’s days; the repeated exodus setting makes guidance a communal passage.
terra: Those who set up rivals lead people away from God’s road and are told that their destination is the Fire, making misdirection and the route’s terminal blaze explicit in one ayah.
terra: God knows those who advance and those who lag behind, directly encompassing every position from the head to the rear of the human line.

terra: God answers Satan by identifying a straight path under His authority and then limiting Satan’s power over His servants; the true road is defined against the would-be misleader waiting beside it.

luna: Lot is told to travel with his family at night, follow their rear, and let no one look back; this supplies the source section's exact rearguard position and forward-only travel. | terra: Lot must travel with his family during part of the night, follow at their rear, and let no one turn around; this is the section’s complete night-caravan arrangement.

luna: The ayah says the straight road is God's to point out, while some ways turn aside; it develops the source section's hidaya as identifying a road and the warning fire as marking a boundary. | terra: The direction of the road rests with God while some roads deviate; this is a close formulation of God assuming responsibility for guidance while identifying wrong branches.

luna: This ayah lays out paths through the land so people may find their way; the next ayah, 16:16, adds markers and the star that orient them, completing this row's road with the source section's sign-fire image. | terra: The earth contains rivers and roads so people may be guided, preparing the terrestrial route whose landmarks and stellar light are named in 16:16.

luna: The ayah pairs road markers (عَلَامَات) with finding direction by a star, a close counterpart to the source section's menār, a sign on the road, and its night-sky guidance. | terra: God places landmarks, and people find their way by the stars; these are the Quran’s explicit counterparts to the fire-marker on a dark road.
terra: The command to call to the Lord’s path with wisdom and good instruction embodies the section’s definition of guidance as gentle indication of ways.
terra: God carries His servant by night between two sanctuaries to show him signs; it is a divinely directed nocturnal journey with a known departure and destination.
terra: The Quran guides to the course that is most upright, giving the revealed warning the practical work of straightening a route.

luna: Night and day are made as signs, with night darkened and day made visible so people can seek provision and reckon time; this explains the source section's contrast between a path visible by day and needing a fire by night. | terra: Night and day are two signs: the night sign is darkened and the day sign made sight-giving, which explains why the route is generally visible by day but needs a beacon at night.
terra: Whoever is blind here is blinder in the Hereafter and further astray from the road, joining failed sight to greater loss of direction.
terra: Those God leaves astray are gathered on their faces, blind, deaf, and dumb, with Hell as refuge; failed guidance, inverted bodily direction, and fire converge.

luna: The ayah describes people who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking His Face; their steady orientation to God extends the source section's Face as the walker's destination. | terra: The Messenger must stay with those seeking their Lord’s face morning and evening and must not turn his eyes away, opposing steadfast orientation to a diverted gaze.
terra: The guilty see the Fire, become certain they are falling into it, and find no turning place away; sight of the fire now confirms the route’s fatal end.
terra: Moses and his companion correct their journey by turning back and retracing their own footprints, showing how a remembered marker restores a lost route.
terra: Every person comes to Hell, by the Lord’s settled decree; the warning fire stands as a boundary all travellers must confront.
terra: God then saves the God-fearing and leaves the wrongdoers kneeling there, distinguishing those kept from the fire’s hold from those abandoned at it.

luna: The source section's literal fire-as-guide scene is explicit: Moses has seen a fire and hopes to find guidance at it (هُدًى); this joins its نَارٌ to a coal, a traveler, and a guide in one moment. | terra: Moses sees a fire during family travel and expects either a firebrand or guidance at it; this is the section’s distant beacon, provision, and road knowledge in one ayah.

luna: Moses reaches the fire and is called by name; this immediate continuation of 20:10 answers the source section's possibility of finding guidance at a fire by making it the place where divine guidance begins. | terra: When Moses comes to the fire he is called, confirming that the light seen at a distance truly directs him to an encounter rather than merely supplying fuel.
terra: The fire has led Moses to the sacred valley, where he is told to remove his sandals; the distant sign thus discloses the exact place to which he was being directed.

luna: God commands Moses to travel by night and makes a dry path through the sea for his people; it joins a guided night journey to a route opened for a traveling group. | terra: Moses is commanded to take God’s servants out by night and strike a dry road through the sea without fearing pursuit; divine direction opens a night-caravan route.
terra: God asks why Moses has hurried ahead of his people, isolating the leader’s forward position before Moses describes the following line.
terra: Moses says his people are close upon his tracks while he has hastened ahead to God; leader, traces, and following company form an explicit caravan order.
terra: After Moses hurries ahead while his people follow his tracks, God tells him that the Samiri has led them astray; the guide’s separation from the line permits a rival leader to divert it.
terra: Whoever follows God’s guidance will neither go astray nor become wretched, making following the guide the protection against losing the road.
terra: Broad passes are set among the mountains so that people may find their way; God makes the route itself legible before any traveller enters it.

luna: God makes prophets leaders guiding by His command; that group being led develops the source section's hadī as the guide who goes ahead of a following caravan. | terra: Abraham’s line is made into leaders guiding by God’s command, another direct formulation of the guide as the community’s divinely authorized front.
terra: Those already promised the best by God are kept far from Hell, supplying the saving distance opposite entering or remaining in the flame.
terra: Those kept far from Hell in 21:101 do not even hear its faintest sound, defining complete removal from the warning fire rather than mere survival within it.
terra: Whoever takes Satan as patron is led astray and guided to the punishment of the Blaze; a corrupt guide directs his follower to the fire as terminus.
terra: The arrogant disputant turns his side to lead others away from God’s road and is promised the punishment of burning, joining bodily orientation, misguidance, and fire.

luna: Its lamp and layered light end with God guiding whom He wills to His light; that makes the source section's dictionary link between نُور and نَار through illumination concrete as a symbol that guides. | terra: God’s light is figured as a lamp kindled in a niche, and the ayah ends with God guiding whom He wills to His light; luminous fire and divine guidance become one sign.
terra: Layered darkness leaves a person barely able to see his own hand, and whoever receives no light from God has no light; it states the beacon scene’s negative limit.

luna: Hell is seen from a distant place; this reverses the source section's traveler seeing a far fire as a useful guide, since here the far-seen fire is itself the threatening destination. | terra: The Blaze sees the deniers from a distant place before they reach it; this reverses the section’s traveller who sees a far fire and chooses how to approach.
terra: The wrongdoer wishes he had taken a road together with the Messenger, expressing salvation as joining the guide’s course.
terra: The false companion led the speaker away from the Reminder after it arrived; it identifies the rival guide who displaced the Messenger’s road desired in 25:27.

terra: The Messenger asks no payment, only that whoever wills take a road to his Lord; lack of recompense, a chosen way, and the Lord as destination closely meet the section’s giver and Godward course.

luna: Night and day succeed one another as a reminder; this adds the recurring alternation that underlies the source section's paired orders of night and day. | terra: God makes night and day successors to one another for whoever wishes to remember or give thanks, supplying an ordered alternation analogous to a continuing procession.
terra: God tells Moses to take His servants out by night because they will be pursued, beginning the guided night procession whose crisis is answered in 26:62.
terra: When the fleeing company fears being overtaken, Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him; guidance is promised at the caravan’s apparent dead end.
terra: At God’s command the sea parts into mountain-like sides, concretely opening the way promised by the guidance of 26:62.
terra: Lot’s entire family is saved except an old woman among those left behind, repeating the boundary between the departing company and the one who remains.

luna: Moses sees a fire and may bring a glowing brand so his family can warm themselves; the source section explicitly sets this reachable, warming fire beside 92:15's ص ل ي root for entering and burning in the other fire. | terra: Moses sees fire and goes for news or a burning brand so his family may warm themselves; تَصْطَلُونَ supplies the section’s near, warming use of the same root whose hell-fire use means entering and burning.

luna: At the fire Moses hears a call and its surroundings are declared blessed; this continuation of 27:7 turns the expected warmth or report into a meeting with the source of guidance. | terra: On reaching the fire Moses hears blessing pronounced on whoever is in it and around it; the ayah sharply distinguishes presence within the fire from presence beside it.
terra: People are asked to notice the night made for rest and the day made sight-giving, the same perceptual alternation presupposed by the signal-fire scene.
terra: Those bringing evil are cast face-first into the fire; the face that should establish a Godward route becomes the point of forced entry at the wrong terminus.
terra: Moses sets his face toward Midian and asks that his Lord guide him to the level road; it is literal travel corrected by divine guidance.

luna: Moses sees fire at the mountain's side while traveling with his family. The source section identifies “side” (جَانِب) as the dictionary root ج ن ب also heard in 92:17's being kept away, setting approach to this fire against distance from the blazing one. | terra: After setting out with his family, Moses sees fire from the side of Sinai and hopes for news or a burning brand; the fire is simultaneously a distant landmark and something brought back to the caravan.

luna: After Moses sees the fire at the mountain's side in 28:29, this ayah places the call from the valley's right side and a blessed spot; it completes the source section's side/fire encounter with a voice that gives direction. | terra: When Moses comes to the fire, the call reaches him from the tree in the blessed spot at the valley’s right side; the distant sign resolves into a precisely located guide.

luna: These leaders invite people to the Fire, a direct reversal of a guide who uses fire to show travelers where the road lies and where it ends. | terra: God makes Pharaoh’s party leaders who call toward the fire, a direct reversal of the guide whose forward position leads travellers to safety.
terra: Praise belongs to God in the first life and the Hereafter, judgment is His, and all return to Him; first, last, rule, and final destination are gathered together.
terra: If God made night perpetual, no other deity could bring light; the thought experiment reveals that every night beacon depends on God’s gift of illumination.
terra: If God made day perpetual, no other deity could bring the night in which people rest; day and night are ordered services rather than rival powers.

luna: God makes night and day for rest and the pursuit of bounty; this gives the source section's two travel modes a repeated Quranic account of their different uses. | terra: God makes night for rest and day for seeking bounty, assigning the two phases their different human modes as the section assigns them different travel conditions.
terra: Everything perishes except God’s face, judgment is His, and all return to Him; the sought direction is also the remaining end beyond the whole road.
terra: The messengers assure Lot that he and his family will be saved except his wife, who is among those remaining behind; the family caravan’s exception is stated before the escape.

luna: Those who strive for God are promised guidance to His ways; this links the source section's seeker of the Lord's Face to the paths that guidance makes known. | terra: Those who strive for God are promised guidance into His paths; divine guidance opens traversable ways for the walkers.
terra: The command belongs to God before and after, a close conceptual parallel to first and last belonging to Him even though the wording uses temporal “before” and “after.”
luna: Sleep at night and seeking bounty by day are signs; this repeats the source section's distinction between a night walker and one who can travel in daylight.

luna: The command to set one's face toward the upright religion uses وَجْه as bodily orientation, matching the source section's image of walking with the Lord's Face as one's direction. | terra: The command to set the face toward the upright religion translates physical orientation into a stable religious course fixed by God’s creation.
terra: Giving relatives, the needy, and the traveller their due is called good for those who desire God’s face, joining provision for a wayfarer to the giver’s true direction.
terra: The alms that increases with God is what is given desiring His face, another direct union of giving and Godward orientation.
terra: The face must be set toward the straight religion before an irreversible day arrives, adding a temporal end-point to the chosen direction.
terra: People follow their fathers’ road despite Satan calling his party toward the Blaze; inherited following becomes a caravan led to the warning fire.
terra: Whoever submits his face to God while doing good grasps the firmest handhold, and the outcome of all affairs is to God; orientation and final arrival coincide.

luna: God makes leaders who guide by His command, again giving the source section's hidaya a human guide at the front of a community. | terra: God makes steadfast believers leaders who guide by His command, explicitly joining forward communal position to delegated divine guidance.
terra: God and the angels bless believers to bring them from darkness into light, preserving the image’s movement from a night state into visibility.
terra: The Messenger is a caller to God and an illuminating lamp, so the guide himself becomes the elevated light toward which travellers can orient.
terra: The people in punishment confess that obedience to their chiefs and great ones led them away from the road; the trusted front rank proves to have been a false guide.

terra: God places clearly visible towns at measured stages along the road and tells the travellers to journey through them safely by nights and days; this is a fully provisioned caravan route whose successive markers make the way knowable.
terra: The people ask for longer distances between their journeys and are then scattered; it reverses the measured, visible, safe itinerary of 34:18 into broken travel and dispersion.
terra: Satan calls his party so that they become companions of the Blaze, a rival caller assembling and leading a company toward fire.

terra: God records what people send ahead and the traces they leave; آثار can include the footprints or effects by which later walkers recognize a trodden course, though the ayah’s claim is broader than literal tracks.
terra: The town’s believer tells his people to follow messengers who ask no payment and are themselves rightly guided; rightful leaders, following, guidance, and freedom from recompense coincide.
terra: The sun cannot overtake the moon and night cannot outstrip day, each moving in its course; the cosmic sequence clarifies an order in which one member does not displace the next.
terra: If God erased their eyes, people could race for the path but could not see it; the ayah states why a road alone is useless without sight-giving light.
terra: God brings fire for people from a green tree and they kindle from it, repeating the practical, divinely provided fire-making scene developed more fully in 56:71–73.
terra: The condemned are ordered to be guided to the road of Hell; guidance vocabulary is deliberately reversed into a procession whose destination is the fire.
terra: The condemned find their fathers already astray, identifying the earlier rank of the false procession before 37:70 describes the descendants’ movement behind it.
terra: The descendants hasten along their fathers’ traces, a vivid instance of speed and precedent supplying no guarantee that the trodden road is right.
terra: Lot and all his family are saved except an old woman among those who stay behind, another compressed recollection of the rearward exception.
luna: The ayah describes night and day wrapping over one another, extending the source section's alternating covered night and disclosed day into a recurring cycle.
terra: A person sets up rivals to mislead from God’s road and is told that his final company is the people of the Fire; false direction determines destination.
terra: The receptive believer proceeds upon a light from his Lord, opposite the hard-hearted; the light supplies a God-given orientation even though no literal road is staged.
terra: God guides by the revealed discourse and leaves the one He sends astray without a guide; it identifies the source of the light described in 39:22.
terra: One who must shield his face from the evil punishment of the Resurrection reverses the upright traveller whose face is freely set toward God.
terra: At final judgment the earth shines with its Lord’s light as the record is set and judgment begins; the journey’s end is staged under divine illumination rather than night darkness.
terra: Disbelievers are driven to Hell in groups, and its keepers ask whether warners had come; a mass procession reaches the fire whose warning was ignored.
terra: The God-fearing are driven in groups to the Garden and welcomed at its opened gates, the contrary destination and reception of the procession in 39:71.
terra: Pharaoh claims that he guides only to the way of right; his false claim supplies the contrary leader against whom the true guide of 40:38 is heard.

luna: Pharaoh tells his people to follow him, claiming to guide them to the right way; unlike the source section's hādī, the guide who goes ahead, 11:98 reveals where this leader actually brings his people. | terra: The believing man commands his people to follow him so that he may guide them to the way of right, enacting the guide who walks ahead.
terra: Inside the Fire the weak remind the arrogant that they were their followers and ask for relief, showing the rear of the procession confronting those it followed.
terra: God makes night for rest and day for seeing, locating the traveller’s changing visibility within divine provision.
terra: Thamud receive guidance but prefer blindness to guidance; the refusal converts a shown road into a chosen inability to see it.

luna: The ayah calls revelation a light by which God guides people to a straight path; it joins the source section's linked نور/نار illumination, guidance, and the road the traveler needs to find. | terra: Revelation is made a light by which God guides, and the Messenger himself guides to a straight path; divine and human guidance are distinguished while sharing one route.
terra: The straight path named in 42:52 is God’s path, and all affairs ultimately proceed to Him; the road’s guide, owner, and terminus coincide.

luna: God makes roads in the earth so people may be guided; the source section defines هداية as making roads known and imagines a sign that lets the traveler find one. | terra: God spreads the earth and places roads in it so people may be guided, presenting physical way-making as a divine act.
terra: Imitators claim they are guided while walking upon their ancestors’ traces; an already-trodden road can therefore be a false guide.
terra: The privileged repeat that they follow ancestral tracks even when a messenger offers better guidance, exposing the danger of mistaking mere precedence for rightful leadership.
terra: Whoever blinds himself to the Reminder is assigned a devil as inseparable companion, establishing the false travelling partner whose route appears in 43:37.
terra: The devil companions bar people from the road while their followers suppose themselves guided, showing how a company can move confidently under a false bearing.
terra: At arrival the deluded follower wishes an east-to-west distance from his companion, using the widest directional separation to expose how disastrous that companionship was.
terra: The hearers are told not to doubt the Hour and to follow the speaker because this is a straight road; eschatological warning becomes an instruction to fall in behind a guide.
terra: Moses is again commanded to travel by night with God’s servants as a pursued company, repeating the night-caravan pattern.
terra: The listening jinn describe the post-Mosaic Book as guiding to truth and to a straight road; revelation supplies both correct knowledge and direction.
terra: Those who turn back after guidance has become clear are enticed by Satan, joining bodily retreat to rejection of a disclosed route.

luna: This ayah says the Hereafter and the first life belong to God, repeating the source section's paired “last and first” order (الآخرة والأولى) and extending its caravan's head-to-tail span to God's sovereignty over both lives. | terra: “To God belong the Hereafter and the first life” mirrors 92:13 almost word for word, grounding the section’s claim that the caravan’s last and first are both His.
luna: The ayah names one who turns away from God's remembrance and seeks only the nearer life; it gives a concrete counter-direction to the source section's traveler moving toward the Lord's Face.
terra: Lot’s family alone is rescued before dawn while the destructive storm strikes his people, preserving the nocturnal family escape from the fuller travel account.
terra: Criminals are dragged on their faces into the fire and told to taste its touch, an extreme reversal of walking face-forward under guidance.
terra: All that is upon the earth passes away while the majestic face of the Lord remains, clarifying why that face can be sought as the road’s enduring end.
terra: The question “Have you considered the fire you kindle?” foregrounds human fire-making before 56:73 assigns that fire its reminder and traveller-provision roles.
terra: God, not the travellers, creates the fire’s tree; this puts the practical signal and provision under the same divine ownership as guidance.
terra: God makes kindled fire a reminder and a provision for desert travellers; it directly confirms the fire’s practical service to people away from settled roads.

luna: The source section uses first/last for both a caravan's ends and the two lives; this ayah applies al-Awwal and al-Akhir to God Himself, shifting that same pair from a created sequence to divine scope. | terra: God is “the First and the Last,” moving the section’s front-and-rear image from what He owns to names by which He is known.
terra: God sends clear signs to His servant so that he may bring people from darkness into light, another explicit revelatory illumination of a human company.

luna: At judgment, believers' light runs before them and at their right; light placed ahead of a moving group develops the source section's image of a guide visible in front. | terra: Believers’ light runs before them and on their right as they move toward their promised destination, giving the caravan a luminous front.

terra: Those left behind ask the believers to wait so they can borrow their light and are told to turn back and seek it; relative position in the procession determines who has the guiding light of 57:12.

luna: God gives believers a light “by which you walk” (تَمْشُونَ بِهِ); this directly extends the source section's traveler whose path is made visible by an external fire into guidance carried along the way. | terra: God promises believers a light by which they walk; the ayah makes illumination an enabling guide for movement rather than merely an object seen.
terra: People are commanded to believe in God, His Messenger, and the light He has sent down, identifying revelation as the communal light to be trusted.
terra: A messenger recites clear signs to bring faithful doers from darkness into light, reiterating the guide’s spoken means of illumination.
terra: Believers are commanded to protect themselves and their families from a Fire, turning warning into responsibility for steering the whole household away from it.

luna: Believers again have light running before them and on their right as they ask God to complete it; this repeated judgment scene makes light a forward guide for travelers toward their destination. | terra: The believers’ light runs before them while they ask God to perfect it, placing divine light at the head of their final journey.
terra: Each company cast into Hell is asked by its keepers whether a warner came to it, directly joining group arrival at fire to the prior warning meant to redirect it.
terra: The arriving company admits that a warner came but was denied, distinguishing absence of guidance from refusal of the warning already given.
terra: God makes the earth manageable, commands people to walk its paths and eat His provision, and names resurrection as the final return; road, sustenance, and terminus are held together.
terra: The ayah asks whether one walking fallen on his face is better guided than one walking upright on a straight road; face, gait, guidance, and route meet in a single comparison.
terra: The object that calls the back-turner in 70:17 is first identified as the Flame, so the later summons is unmistakably a call issued by fire.
terra: The Flame calls the person who turned his back and withdrew, making the warning fire itself summon the traveller whose bodily direction is away from guidance.
terra: People emerge from graves rushing toward a raised goal or marker as if racing to it; the road-marker scene reappears at resurrection with an ominous destination rather than a saving beacon.

luna: The ayah invites whoever wills to take a way to his Lord; it makes explicit the path-to-the-Lord relation that the source section develops from seeking the Lord's Face. | terra: The reminder lets whoever wills take a road to his Lord, stating the warning’s purpose as a freely chosen Godward route.

luna: The source section points out the denier's turn-away action; this ayah uses the same turning-away verb after a man considers the reminder, opposing a traveler who stays oriented toward guidance.
terra: The great fire just described is a warning to humankind; it supplies the explicit warning function for the forward-or-backward choice in 74:37.
terra: Immediately after the fire is called a warning, the ayah addresses whoever wishes to advance or fall behind; the warning fire orders the procession by direction.
terra: On that day the human being is informed of what he sent ahead and what he left behind, transferring front-and-rear language from a caravan’s positions to the temporal reach of deeds.
terra: Some faces on that day are radiant, preparing the direct Godward gaze stated in 75:23 as the fulfilment of their orientation.
terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, giving the sought Godward direction an eschatological completion.

luna: The way is shown to the human being, who may respond gratefully or reject it; this makes explicit the traveler's response to guidance that the source section's road-sign image implies. | terra: God guides the human being to the road and leaves a real response between gratitude and ingratitude; showing the route does not erase the traveller’s choice.

luna: The speakers say they feed others only for the Face of God (لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ), a direct parallel to the source section's Face as the intention that directs one's path. | terra: The feeders declare that they feed solely for God’s face and want neither repayment nor thanks, directly matching 92:19–20’s unrequited giving for the Lord’s face.

luna: This repeated formulation again offers a way to the Lord, clarifying that the source section's Face-seeking image has a destination as well as a direction. | terra: The same reminder formula again invites whoever wills to take a road to the Lord, a repeated direct formulation of warning as wayfinding.
luna: Night is made a covering, giving another direct formulation of the source section's darkened travel scene in which a fire is needed to disclose the road.
luna: Day is made for livelihood, adding a repeated Quranic night/day division to the source section's contrast between night travel and the broad visibility of day.
terra: Moses asks Pharaoh whether he will purify himself and let Moses guide him to his Lord so that he may fear; a human guide offers a Godward road through warning.

terra: Pharaoh is seized for the punishment of “the last and the first”; the precise pair is reused in a punitive sense whose referents are debated, so it marks a lexical boundary rather than a clear caravan scene.
terra: Every soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind, repeating the moral secondary sense of a divinely known front and rear.
terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting than the nearer life, adding permanence and value to the section’s paired first and last stages.

luna: God guides the human being to the two paths (النَّجْدَيْنِ); the fork makes the source section's guide and warning fire a choice of direction rather than a general religious theme. | terra: God shows the human being the two high roads, a compact image of divinely disclosed alternative routes.
luna: Daylight's disclosure in this oath directly echoes the source section's day appearing into broad light, when travelers need no guiding fire.
luna: Night's covering in this paired oath directly echoes the source section's darkened road, when the distant fire becomes a guide.
terra: The Hereafter is better than the first life, retaining the paired terms while adding an evaluative asymmetry absent from the section’s image of one divinely owned line.
terra: God finds the Prophet without the way and guides him; although no literal journey is staged, guidance is remembered as God’s personal recovery of one lacking direction.
